clue.text: Guy seeking to raise temperature on stairs is struggling

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of the two words before it are thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man trying to warm up a stairwell is having a hard time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: someone who raises the temperature by setting fires.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser deliberately starts blazes, which certainly makes things hotter.

clue.text: Charge account linked to employment

parts.note: use means employment

explanation.surface: A bill itemised by how much the services were used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks financial, matching 'account', but it means to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to formally allege wrongdoing.

clue.text: Good comic's trick taking soldiers in

indicators.note: taking ... in means the trick holds the soldiers inside it
in completes the phrase taking in, signalling one piece inside another

parts.note: a scam is a trick or swindle
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine involves recruiting soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hilarious is informally called a scream.

clue.text: Olives uncle in EU prepared in different way maybe?

definitions.text: Olives uncle in EU prepared in different way maybe?

indicators.note: prepared in a different way suggests the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative in Europe serves olives in a novel fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1970s cooking style presented food lightly and inventively, preparing dishes differently.

clue.text: Part of Hamlet understood by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for understood is heard, not spelt

parts.note: seen can mean understood, as in I see

explanation.surface: A remark that a bit of Shakespeare's play makes sense when heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays are divided into acts and their subdivisions, one stage episode each.

clue.text: Uniform (Royal), man is pressing

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man in royal uniform is putting on pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is one demanding immediate attention.

clue.text: Moving away, I mixed with a girl racer in this?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'racer in this? (7,8)', cut short in OCR with no scan; the blog gives 'Moving away, I mixed with a girl racer in this?', an anagram of AWAY I A GIRL RACER, but the held text cannot be mended without a scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: Moving away, I mixed with a girl racer in this?

clue.text: Kitchen item, for example, that sorts grime out over time

indicators.note: sorts ... out means the letters are put in a new order
out completes sorts out, the rearranging signal

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget that cleans off dirt over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' links in this down clue; the T for 'time' is rearranged with GRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: This small hourglass measures the minutes for boiling breakfast.

clue.text: Those people welcoming girl climbing in Greek region

indicators.note: welcoming means the word for those people holds the other piece inside

parts.note: they means those people

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word for girl is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: People welcome a young woman climbing in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a historic area of central mainland Greece.

clue.text: Have drink (or two!) at opening of latest airport feature?

parts.note: to carouse is to drink heavily and merrily

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken from the word latest

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a few drinks at the opening of the newest airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a carousel is where luggage circulates at an airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage reclaim uses a rotating belt from which travellers collect their luggage.

clue.text: Objection on return home, Government delight cut short

indicators.note: on return means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lopped off the word for delight

parts.note: glee is delight

explanation.surface: A complaint about the government spoiling one's homecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggle is a minor complaint or nagging doubt.

clue.text: He presents bill that shows drink a Rector brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the letters go inside the word for drink

parts.note: beer is a drink

explanation.surface: A man presents a bill showing drinks bought for the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever carries and hands over a cheque or banknote is its holder.

clue.text: Financial interest small and appropriate

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it

explanation.surface: A modest and fitting share in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a holding in a business gives you money riding on its success.

clue.text: Plant seeds while husband's away on a trip

indicators.note: letters on a trip travel about and land in a new order
away means the letter for husband is taken out of the fodder

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone sows seeds while their husband is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing H from SEEDS WHILE leaves SEEDSWILE, which 'on a trip' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The edelweiss is a small white-flowered Alpine species.

clue.text: Rung by rebel, it'll free?

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose to settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A bell sounded by an insurgent will set people free.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberty Bell in Philadelphia is a symbol of American independence, so the surface fits the answer; 'Rung' defines it loosely as a thing that is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous cracked bell in Philadelphia was struck to mark independence, a thing that is sounded by striking.

clue.text: Outlawed group given hearing

indicators.note: given a hearing says the word for group is heard rather than read

parts.note: a band is a group

explanation.surface: A banned musical group gets its day in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prohibited is forbidden by law or rule.

clue.text: From country like Faroes, so it's said

explanation.surface: A nationality compared to islanders of the North Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: Faroes said aloud sounds like Pharaohs, the ancient rulers of the Nile kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses point to the Nile nation: a native of it, and akin to its ancient kings whose title sounds like Faroes.

clue.text: Warn team about Dennis?

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to the team about someone called Dennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Waterman was a British actor, star of the TV series The Sweeney and Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: The British television actor Dennis is known by this surname, so the name is a definition by example.

clue.text: Island song mature lady is able to put on initially

indicators.note: put on initially means these pieces are placed before the song

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, an older woman
can means is able
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: An older woman is able to put on a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran Canaria is one of Spain's Canary Islands off West Africa.

clue.text: French star crude perhaps during summer there

indicators.note: during means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: ete is French for summer, there pointing back to France
crude oil, so crude is an example of oil

explanation.surface: A French celebrity behaves crudely during the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the word for a celestial body or a celebrity is this.

clue.text: Boy's terse to some extent — he gives little away

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A curt lad who reveals almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-lipped, secretive person is likened to a shellfish that stays shut.

clue.text: Politician I'd introduced to host

indicators.note: introduced to means the short form for I'd goes inside the word for host

parts.note: to present a show is to host it
I'd without its apostrophe gives these letters

explanation.surface: A politician says he was introduced to the host.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of state such as the US leader is an elected political figure.

clue.text: Dance beat's not half good!

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the word good is used

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic remark that a dance beat is really good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' looks like the British emphatic meaning very much, but here it halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom routine.

clue.text: Irritable artist refusing drink at Gallery's close

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
TT means teetotal, refusing alcohol

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here of Gallery

explanation.surface: A grumpy painter turns down a drink as the gallery closes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for bad-tempered or cross.

clue.text: Like some verse in Athens, mainly bucolic (in couplets primarily)

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A description of pastoral Greek poetry written in rhyming pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry built from iambs, feet of short then long syllables, is described this way.

clue.text: One making records reproduced in new atlas

indicators.note: reproduced suggests the letters are remade in a different order

explanation.surface: Maps reproduced in a fresh edition of an atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes year-by-year historical accounts.

clue.text: Port worker visiting North East Sweden

indicators.note: visiting means the worker goes inside the compass and country letters

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A dock labourer travels to northeastern Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a French city on the Loire with a historic harbour.

clue.text: Anxiety about tiresome fellow, first to last — one from the past

indicators.note: about means the word for anxiety goes around the other piece

parts.note: fear is anxiety

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter moves to the end of the word for a tiresome fellow

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

explanation.surface: Worry about a tedious man, an ancestor perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the opening letter of the tiresome fellow to the end; 'about' then puts the result inside the word for anxiety. The dash is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is someone in your family line who lived long ago.
